# The actual centroid-hull contraction: a surface Jensen defect and a strict ascent calibration

The centroid hull is used here as a compatible deformation target, not as
a proposed center selector. The archived centroid-hull selector is false.
This note proves the actual first variation, identifies its exact sign
under a normal-preserving physical dual, and gives an actual buffered
family where the deformation strictly INCREASES normalized depth despite
full-space volume transport and global concave-parameter optimality.
That family is not a joint body minimum; its reverse path is an actual
descent. A separate planar example shows why reversal is not generally
compatible, even under every strict closed-minor mass quota.

## 1. An actual nested compatible path

Let C be the canonical hull of positive compatible convex d-fibers K_z
on a finite complete base P. Write g_z for their ordinary centroids and

    D=conv{(z,g_z):z in P},    D_z={X:(z,X) in D}.

Convexity gives D subset C, and D_z contains g_z. For 0<=t<1 put

    K_z(t)=(1-t)K_z+t D_z.                              (1)

The family is compatible: for any anchored relation q=sum lambda_z z,
both sum lambda K_z subset K_q and sum lambda D_z subset D_q hold, so
the corresponding inclusion holds for (1). Its canonical hull therefore
has exactly the displayed sampled fibers. This is fiberwise Minkowski
interpolation; no identity with a full ambient Minkowski interpolation
at different base coordinates is presumed.

Since D_z subset K_z, these fibers are nested in t. Since g_z in D_z,
they contain g_z+(1-t)(K_z-g_z), hence are positive for t<1 with common
inballs locally in t. Possible lower dimension at t=1 is irrelevant.
The usual rational perpendicular thickening handles deficient base rank.

The support functions satisfy the exact uniform identity

    h_Kz(t)(n)=h_Kz(n)-t[h_Kz(n)-h_Dz(n)].               (2)

At almost every old boundary point X, with its unique outward unit normal
n_z(X), the actual inward normal speed is

    v_z(X)=h_Kz(n_z)-h_Dz(n_z)>=0.                     (3)

Here (3) is stronger than a merely pointwise support derivative. To
justify it, fix a common interior radial origin in each fiber. The radial
function is the minimum of h_t(n)/(n.omega) over positive denominators.
Uniform support convergence, the inball and outer bound make the radial
shift O(t) uniformly. At an old regular boundary point every convergent
sequence of active normal minimizers tends to its unique old normal.
The minimum-envelope difference quotient then gives (3). The uniform
O(t) bound permits radial-shell dominated convergence. Thus total first
loss is integral v dS, and each fixed regular cap has first loss
integral_boundary 1_H v dS. Supporting-cap selectors require the separate
directional theory and are not silently linearized here.

This does not contradict the archived Minkowski-response obstruction:
there the varying bodies had nonuniform, discontinuous limiting support
derivatives. In (2) the derivative is a fixed continuous support-function
difference on the whole normal sphere.

## 2. Exact physical response and its surface meaning

Use the regular same-separator density Xi and force F_z from
`candidate 8f0725a173821a00`.
Define the nonnegative repair term

    R_z(n)=h_Dz(n)-n.g_z>=0.

Because v_z=n.(X-g_z)-R_z(n), its exact response is

    R_centroid = integral_boundary Xi v
          =-sum_z g_z.F_z-integral_boundary Xi R_z(n). (4)

Neither the pointwise nonnegativity of R_z nor the full-space volume
martingale signs the last integral, because Xi is signed and surface
weighted. In particular, the volume martingale is not a license to
remove this correction.

There is a precise conclusion if the physical dual is available in its
NORMAL-PRESERVING form. Let pi_S couple the Xi-positive and Xi-negative
normal-bundle surface marginals, preserve n, have full physical row
barycenters, and retain actual global support-plane contact. These are
the audited normal-bundle hypotheses, not consequences of an unlabelled
volume coupling. At each row, actual support contact gives

    h_Kz(n)=E[h_KZ'(n)|z,X,n].                         (5)

For fixed n, h_Dz(n) is a concave function of the real base z: it is
the upper boundary of the projection of D under (z,X)->(z,n.X).
Equivalently,

 h_Dz(n)=max{sum_p lambda_p n.g_p:
                  lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda p=z}.

Hence the row barycenter property gives a nonnegative Jensen defect

    J_D=integral [h_Dz(n)-E(h_DZ'(n)|z,X,n)] dmu_S>=0.

Using (5), the response in (4) is EXACTLY

    R_centroid=-J_D<=0,                                (6)
    integral Xi R_z(n)=J_D-sum_z g_z.F_z.               (7)

Thus at such a dual certificate this particular inward path is a
concave-base support test, with the sign expected at a minimum. It is not
a new guaranteed descent. Equality holds precisely when every positive
surface row has equality for this centroid support roof. This confines
that row to an affine contact cell of the roof; it does not force one
global affine centroid graph. No normals or contact labels from pi_S have
been assigned to the separate volume coupling.

## 3. A genuine buffered critical family with full volume transport

Take n=d=1 and the actual complete three-fiber family

    P={-1,0,1},   K_-=K_+=[-1,1],   K_0=[-1,7].        (8)

The midpoint inclusion is immediate. The total mass, within-fiber
covariance, and full mixed centroid are

    M=12,    Sigma=11/3,    bar w=(0,2).

Set L=1, use the unpenalized invariant buffer, and choose epsilon so that

    delta=epsilon sqrt(55/24),       0<delta<=1/10.     (9)

For an interval [l,r] its exact energy is

    E(y)=4(y-l)(r-y)/(r-l).

Consequently at Y=(0,2), E_0(2)=15/2, and delta is its physical buffer.
The ACTUAL global maximum buffered raw depth is

    Q=5+delta,   beta=(5+delta)/12,                     (10)

uniquely attained at Y. Here are all-direction details.

For a positive continuous normal, the middle upper cap through the shifted
level 2-delta already has length 5+delta; the two endpoint contributions
are nonnegative. The horizontal cap has both endpoint traces empty and
attains this value. For a negative continuous normal the middle captured
length is 3+delta. The two identical symmetric endpoint intervals have
opposite base shifts and threshold average 2+delta>0; their lower-cap
lengths sum to at least 2. This follows directly by pairing x in one
interval with -x in the other. A sufficiently large tilt makes one full
and one empty, attaining 2. Pure-base caps at base zero have mass at least
10. Thus every closed halfspace gives at least (10), and two explicit
regular critical directions are

    X>=2-delta,        -X+4z>=-2-delta.                (11)

The first excludes both endpoints; the second includes the right endpoint
fully and excludes the left one, with strict status gaps. Both own cuts
are proper. Endpoint bases have pure-base upper bound 2<Q.

To prove uniqueness and the global upper bound on the whole middle fiber,
write delta(y)=epsilon sqrt(Sigma E_0(y)/M). It is strictly concave inside
[-1,7], continuous with boundary value zero, and

    delta(2)=delta,    delta'(2)=delta/15.

Any middle mark of buffered depth at least Q must satisfy the right
quantile inequalities of both fixed directions (11):

    y-delta(y)<=2-delta,
    -y-delta(y)<=-2-delta.

Weight them by

    rho_+=(1+delta/15)/2,   rho_-=(1-delta/15)/2.        (12)

They imply (delta/15)(y-2)<=delta(y)-delta. Strict concavity gives the
reverse strict inequality unless y=2. The proper traces at (11) ensure
that their right mass-Q quantiles are the displayed thresholds, including
all other possible candidate statuses. This proves the claim without a
restriction to a sampled tilt menu.

Moreover L=1 is a GLOBAL optimizer over all positive concave full-space
weights with geometric normalization on this fixed body. Indeed any such
L obeys

    L(Y)>= (1/M) integral_S L dm
                       >=exp[(1/M)integral_S log L dm]=1.

Its buffer at the actual mark Y can only increase, so its maximum depth
cannot be below Q. The full-space volume certificate is exact:
delta_Y is in convex order below dm/M because the latter's full mean is
Y. It is L-tight and has the sole continuous gradient label c=0. Thus
the failure below is not attributable to a missing parameter mean or to
using only a base-volume transport. It is still NOT a joint body minimum.
The middle mass is 8>M/2=6, so this calibration also lies outside the
strict-singleton-quota bad-minimum regime. The separate reversal
obstruction in Section 5 does satisfy all strict proper-minor quotas.

## 4. The centroid-hull path strictly raises the exact global depth

Here g_-=g_+=0 and g_0=3, so D_-=D_+={0}, D_0=[0,3]. Formula (1) is

    K_-(t)=K_+(t)=[-1+t,1-t],
    K_0(t)=[-1+t,7-4t],
    M(t)=12-9t.                                       (13)

Keep epsilon and raw L=1 fixed, and update the actual M and covariance.
For all sufficiently small signed t, the exact global maximizing mark is
y(t)=2-t/2 and

    Q(t)=5-7t/2+delta(t),
    delta(t)=epsilon sqrt[Sigma(t)E_t(y(t))/M(t)],
    Sigma(t)=[2(2-2t)^3+(8-5t)^3]/[12(12-9t)],
    E_t(y(t))=4(3-3t/2)(5-7t/2)/(8-5t).                (14)

The proof from Section 3 persists: the two strict endpoint-status gaps
remain, the two own captured masses coincide at y(t), and the derivative
of the strictly concave buffer there has magnitude less than one. Its
two positive quantile weights again prove the global upper bound and
uniqueness. Endpoint atomic bounds remain strictly smaller. Therefore
(14) is an actual optimized depth formula, not just a fixed-cap response.

Differentiating these exact expressions gives

    E'/E=-23/40,    Sigma'/Sigma=-51/44,    M'/M=-3/4,
    delta'=-433 delta/880,
    beta'(0)=1/48+227 delta/10560 >0.                  (15)

The density identity checks the same effect. Its total coareas are equal,
so theta=rho from (12), the response coefficient e=Delta=delta, and the
source energy normalizer is a=1/15. Every F_z is zero: only the middle
has proper sections, whose weighted normal sum delta/15 cancels its
energy flux. The only nonzero geometric repair occurs at the lower
middle endpoint X=-1, where R_0=3. Direct evaluation of (18) in the
log-flux source gives

    Xi_0(-1)=1/12+227 delta/2640,
    integral Xi R_z=1/4+227 delta/880,
    R_centroid=-(1/4+227 delta/880)=-M beta'(0).         (16)

For the concrete rational choice delta=1/10, epsilon^2=6/1375,

    Q=51/10, beta=17/40,
    beta'(0)=809/35200, R_centroid=-2427/8800.

Thus even genuine global criticality and the full-space volume certificate
do not cancel the repair term. No physical surface-dual certificate at a
joint shape minimum is asserted for this example.

In fact (13) remains positive and compatible for NEGATIVE t near zero:
the endpoint interval and the middle have exactly the same lower endpoint,
and the middle upper support remains strictly larger. Hence negative t
gives actual strict descent by (15). This explicitly explains why the
calibration is not a joint minimum.

## 5. Reversal fails in actual planar geometry, even with strict quotas

The following root-supplied exact example prevents extrapolating the
preceding reverse feasibility. At bases -1 and 1 put

    A=B=[-1,1] times [-3,0],       |A|=|B|=6,

and at zero put

    K=conv{(-2,0),(2,0),(1,-3),(-1,-3)},  |K|=9.

Its horizontal section width is 4+(2/3)y, so its centroid is (0,-4/3).
The endpoint centroids are (0,-3/2). The family is actual because A subset K.
All singleton masses are strictly below M/2=21/2, and adjacent two-point
minors have mass15<21; these exhaust the proper closed minors with more
than one point. Thus every proper closed-minor quota is strict.

For n=(0,1), the midpoint support constraint of K is TIGHT:

    h_K(n)=h_A(n)=h_B(n)=0.

But the centroid hull has

    h_D0(n)=-4/3 > -3/2=[h_D-(n)+h_D+(n)]/2.           (17)

The proposed reverse support values h_K+t(h_K-h_D) therefore give upper
endpoint support 3t/2 and middle upper support at most 4t/3. The endpoint
midpoint violates the target cut for every t>0. This remains an obstruction
if the individual reverse bodies are defined by their full outward Wulff
intersections: the endpoint D fibers are points, so those endpoint bodies
are exact homothetic expansions, while the displayed middle upper cut is
still imposed. All individual reverse bodies contain their old body, but
the family is incompatible.

Thus flatness of the centroid roof on a tight body-support relation is a
real extra condition. It does not follow from compatibility, centroids,
or strict mass quotas. The positive contraction is always actual; a
signed two-way argument cannot be imported from it without this missing
contact control.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_centroid_hull_response_slab_recovery.py` passes
1,241 exact response, actual-cap, covariance, and compatibility checks.
The all-direction and all-mark claims use the proofs above; sampled
tilt checks are only an independent arithmetic check of those formulas.
